summary: Pre-dawn desert, the tower and a countdown.

paragraphs.text: Trinity, the first nuclear explosion, was set for {{date_time}} at {{place}}. The device, nicknamed the Gadget, sat in a steel cab on top of a {{tower_height}} tower.

Observers waited in shelters {{shelter_dist}} from the tower. The base camp was {{base_camp_dist}} away. Out here the desert floor is flat for tens of kilometres, so the tower is a thin line against the mountains.
The clock counts down from ten seconds. As it does, the view closes in from the whole test site to the cab at the top of the tower.
In the last second the view passes through the cab wall to the Gadget itself. The next chapter opens it up, layer by layer.

events.detail: The whole site in one view: tower, observer shelters at {{shelter_dist}} and base camp at {{base_camp_dist}}.
One steady camera move from the whole site to the top of the tower, while the clock runs down.
The view passes through the wall of the shot cab to the device inside.
The detonators fire. This instant is T = 0; the officially recorded time is {{date_time}}.
